standard_prerequisites: A consistent axiomatizable theory T extending Q, and the Rosser derivability predicate, which says that there is a proof of the sentence in T and no shorter refutation of it, built from the proof predicate Prf_T and the refutation predicate Refut_T, both represented in Q.

The bounded-quantifier collapse available in Q (the less-nsucc lemma of the representability unit): from Q-proofs of not-phi(k) for each k below n, Q proves the bounded universal statement for all z below the numeral of n.
The fixed-point lemma for Q, giving a sentence R_T with Q proving R_T iff not Rosser-provable of its own Godel number.
The fact that in a consistent T no k below the Godel number of an actual derivation can be the Godel number of a derivation of the negated sentence.
core_obligations: Show T does not derive R_T: assuming a derivation with Godel number n, the representability of Prf_T and of Refut_T plus the bounded collapse yield a Q-proof of the Rosser provability of R_T, hence via the fixed-point equation a Q-proof, hence a T-proof, of not R_T, contradicting consistency.

Show T does not derive not R_T: assuming a derivation of not R_T with Godel number n, each smaller k fails to derive R_T (consistency) and fails to derive not R_T (else T is inconsistent), so the Rosser provability of not R_T holds, and the fixed-point equation together with the shorter-refutation ordering forces T to derive R_T, again contradicting consistency.
proof_roadmap: Set up the two-sided argument: the same fixed-point equation is used in both directions, with the shorter-refutation ordering doing the work that omega-consistency did in the Godel case.

Direction one: a derivation of R_T of Godel number n makes the Rosser predicate true of the Godel number of R_T; the fixed-point equation converts this into a derivation of the negation, contradicting consistency.

Direction two: a derivation of the negation of R_T of Godel number n leaves every smaller k a non-refutation; the bounded collapse produces the negated Rosser provability of the negation, which the fixed-point equation turns into a derivation of R_T; consistency is contradicted either way.
difficulty_reason: A two-direction diagonal argument where the Rosser ordering replaces omega-consistency; each direction needs the representability facts, the bounded-quantifier collapse, and careful bookkeeping of which side the fixed-point equation is applied to.
